source: Minchat Shai on Gen 7:23 (Or Torah; Rashi; Mizrachi)
claim_en: וימח ("and He ERASED," 7:23) — the precise manuscripts: mem SOFT (no dagesh, the doubling dot) — the simple active stem, "He erased all the standing." Minchat Shai's warning: read with dagesh it becomes the passive — "the Enemy of the Holy One [the euphemism] was erased with all the standing" — "and one must be exceedingly careful"; Gur Aryeh's dagesh-books are called corrupt. SNAPSHOT: mem+vowel contiguous, no dot — the careful reading.

וימחו ("and they were erased" — the passive, correctly, of the creatures) — tifcha (a pause accent) on the word. SNAPSHOT agrees: the active erasing and the passive being-erased sit eight words apart, distinguished by one dot the careful books refuse.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 7:23 (Or Torah; Masorah note)
claim_en: וישאר ("and there was LEFT only Noah") — darga (the stair-step accent) on the shin in the precise books; the manuscript Masorah marks the word unique-and-first-stressed. SNAPSHOT: darga.

וישאר — the alef with SEGOL (short e-vowel), "as is right, for were it end-stressed the alef would carry tsere, like ותשאר" (Ruth's clause): the stress-position argument locked at the vowel. SNAPSHOT: segol.
